title: Harmonograph
description: A sheet of warm white paper on the table of a three-pendulum harmonograph. Two pendulums swing a steel pen arm from a brass gimbal at nearly two to three (three to four on the next sheet), a third circles the table and the paper beneath it, and the single line they draw winds inward as the swing decays, thinning where the pen runs fast and darkening where it slows. Take the pen arm, pull it out and let go, or take the paper and throw the table: the pen lifts, comes down on the swing you gave it, and the previous figure settles back into the sheet as a faint ghost. The nib lifts itself once the swing has wound in, so the centre stays open, and you can hear it on the paper. Double-click to tear the sheet off the pad and start a fresh one.
intent: From the Vertigo titles (Saul Bass and John Whitney, 1958, https://artofthetitle.com/title/vertigo): machine-drawn Lissajous figures made with total precision. Here the machine is a real damped three-pendulum harmonograph, and the paper is the object.
